steps.note: S1.2.1 gives rows 0-1 subtracting Ja+Rc, rows 2-5 adding R(c+Gx)+J(a+Vx), rows 6-7 restoring c,a, and the net change (JV+RG)x independent of a,c, as at 744-750.
S1.2.2 states the bit central coefficient |S cap T| mod 2, side wires cancelling exactly the intersection-one cases, zero/two intersections already zero, self coefficient one.
S1.2.3 states the complex central coefficient (|S cap T|-1)/2 cancelled by the side term for intersections zero and two, intersection one contributing zero, self coefficient one.
S1.2.4 gives the three stages (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x) with forward, inverse, forward invocations, and S1.2/S1.2.1 state that each invocation restores its scratch wires.

The plan names residual dimensions (S1.4.1 method) and says every edge joins comparable labels (S1.4.1.5), but never gives the per-edge residual table (B tensor t_X-perp of dimension (a-1)(h-1), P tensor F of dimension h, etc.).

S1.4.1.4 (quoting the label construction at line 953) gives the inclusion P tensor <t_X> inside P tensor t_Y-perp from t_X perp t_Y, but not the side edge 2->5 residual: the complement <t_X,t_Y>-perp of dimension h-2.
The plan states that center 3->4 is the only decreasing edge, losing h; sources N, sinks Wm-N, signed telescoping Wm-2N; Ic decreasing edges with L=Ich and absolute sum Wm-2N+2L.

S1.4.1.7b states that over F2 every nonzero residual is nondegenerate and nonalternating (it contains a norm-one unit) and so has an orthonormal basis, with alternating planes absorbed via w+a, w+b, w+a+b.
S1.4.1.7c gives L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539 exactly.

S1.4.1.9.2 derives additivity of weight mod 4 for orthogonal vectors from the wt(z+w) formula; S1.4.1.9's method and motivation decompose the phase difference over an orthonormal residual basis into one-vector phases, and S1.4.1.9.3 gives each v the coefficient wt(v).
S1.4.1.9.3 states that wt(v) is odd, that the phase is i^{eps[v.x]} = (1+i^eps)/2 + (1-i^eps)/2 (-1)^{v.x}, and that conjugation by H diag(1,-1) H = X turns it into aI+bX_v or its inverse.

S1.4.1.9 gives one kernel per residual basis vector with s_c in total, and S1.4.4.1.4/S1.4.4.1.7 give each residual direction as one tensored factor (C^{eps_h})^{tensor f} across the f columns, s_c child calls in all (paper 1880-1906).

S1.4.4.1.9 restates the proposition (line 1226) and adds that C=iZC^{-1}Z turns the 27 inverse factors on X_a->Y_a forward, but omits the endpoint frames (zero label I, full label C^{tensor m}), only names the corrections without Z_{a,k} before and i^{27k}Z_{a,k} after, and does not mention negating the X outputs.
The plan states both loss ratios are below 1/2, giving deficits N-2L_b>0 and 2N-2L_c>0 and hence s<Wm for both networks.
The plan states both deficits exceed 20*2^-50, log m<20 gives m^{1-2^-50} > m(1-20*2^-50) > m(1-eta), and hence s/W < m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^-50.

S1.4.3.1.2 gives the elimination: pivot at the topmost nonzero row's rightmost entry, lower-triangular clearing left and below, delete and repeat, each step isolating a rank-one block; S1.4.3.1.1 says Pi has exactly a ones.

S1.4.3.1.3 chooses a prime q avoiding all denominators and diagonal numerators, so the factors work over Z/q^b with unit diagonals (the shear stated over Z/q^bZ in S1.4.3.1); this is a compressed but faithful form of the finite-table prime choice.
S1.4.3.1.3 states that a lower triangular transformation costs O(V), updating coordinates in descending physical order by a diagonal unit plus a fixed combination of earlier coordinates.
S1.4.3.1.4-5 give D_j<-D_j+H_i, interchange, D_j<-H_i-D_j taking (h,d) to (h+d,d), one interchange per one of Pi, a in all.

The plan gives E=64(W+m+1)^3, B=s+E, nu through B<=m^nu, C_1=max{20,nu+3}=20, Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}), and C_0 through 128mB^2 d^{nu+3} <= C_0 d^{C_1}; C_0=128mB^2 and nu=11 are not written out explicitly.

S1.4.4.4.1 gives A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E at internal nodes and A(e)<=8e at leaves, with E bounding scalar gates 24W^3, child corrections 4s and bank corrections; S1.4.4.4.2 explains the use of s rather than s/W.
The plan gives sx+E<=Bx, B^{k+1}<=B^2 d^nu, A(e)<=8B^2 d^{nu+1}, and the total below 128mB^2 d^{nu+3} <= C_0 d^{C_1}.
S1.4.4.4.6-7 state that depth ell gives values in 2^{-(p+ell)}Z[i] of modulus at most 2^ell, that p+Delta fractional and Delta+3 integer bits are exact, and that eps*C_1<1 gives Delta=o(p).
S1.4.4.5.3 states that every row of H has absolute row sum one, so disks are preserved and the single truncation errs by less than sqrt2 2^-p.

summary: P03 states 23 of 26 sub-steps. Bank exchange 4/4, residual budget 3/5, phase interface 3/4, rank saving 4/4, matrix shear 4/4, simultaneous layer 5/5. Absent: L1 (no per-edge residual table), L2 (inclusion stated but not the h-2 complement on side edge 2->5), P4 (endpoint frames I and C^{tensor m} and the Z_{a,k}, i^{27k}Z_{a,k} corrections not given). Nothing is stated contrary to the paper.
